body:
* **ARBA rule (ID and label):**
ARBA00022801/ARBA00022670/ARBA00022825

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Dmel genes/Proteins:
Q8SXS2	FBgn0051337	CG31337	
B7Z0L3	FBgn0051266	CG31266

Q9VXC6	FBgn0030776	CG4653	


* **Description of issue**
ARBA00022801 -> keyword [Hydrolase](https://www.uniprot.org/keywords/KW-0378) -> [hydrolase activity (GO:0016787)](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/term/GO:0016787)
ARBA00022670 -> keyword [Protease](https://www.uniprot.org/keywords/KW-0645) -> [peptidase activity (GO:0008233)](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/term/GO:0008233)
ARBA00022825 -> keyword [Serine protease](https://www.uniprot.org/keywords/KW-0720) ->  serine-type peptidase activity (GO:0008236)

All the proteins listed above get all three (redundant) keywords and resulting GO terms.

For Q8SXS2, it's because of the match to:
InterPro signature	IPR022700	Proteinase, regulatory CLIP domain &
InterPro signature	IPR038565	Proteinase, regulatory CLIP domain superfamily (parent of above!)
These domains are defined as 'regulatory domains' so shouldn't be used to assign a catalytic activity.

For all the others, the match is due to:
InterPro signature	IPR050430 (Peptidase S1 family serine proteases) & taxon	Ecdysozoa
or
a FunFam match.
But all of them are pseudopeptidases with a manual GO annotation of "NOT serine-type endopeptidase activity | IKR)"
